newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rising costs force Brazil soluble company to move.
newsitem.headline: Rising costs force Brazil soluble company to move.

text.p: Brazil soluble coffee maker Macsol S.A Manufatura de Cafe Soluvel is transferring its production facilities to Cornelio Procopio, Parana state, from Campinas in Sao Paulo, a company spokeswoman said.
The Campinas factory stopped operating at the beginning of last month because of losses caused by high raw material costs and costs of production, a company statement said.
Macsol then decided to re-locate to Cornelio Procopio in search of economic viability.
Equipment is currently being transferred to the new production unit and the unit should hopefully be up and running in about three months, the spokeswoman said.
Macsol is 51 percent owned by Iguacu Cafe Soluvel and 49 percent by Coca-Cola Brazil, a division of the Coca-Cola Co, the spokeswoman said.

Iguacu, the country's third largest soluble coffee exporter, already has units in the region which should help Macsol to cut costs, said Mauro Malta, executive secretary of the Brazilian Soluble Coffee Industry (ABICS).
Local business daily Gazeta Mercantil said the new factory would produce 1,600 tonnes a year, of which 1,300 tonnes would be destined for the export market.
Macsol's exports in 1996 totaled 1,600 tonnes out of total Brazilian overseas sales of 58,050 tonnes soluble coffee, Malta said.
"But what is important in Macsol's case is not the quantity but the fact that it is a producer of high quality soluble coffee as it is freeze-dried," Malta said.
"This is a serious thing for them to have to move the factory," he added.
The government is currently discussing with soluble producers and other sectorial representatives to see if there are ways to ensure the soluble industry does not lose its competitiveness.
At the moment, Brazilian soluble coffee producers are having to pay higher prices internally for coffee than other soluble producers outside of Brazil.
Because of the current problems, seven of the country's 11 producers are currently on collective holidays, Malta said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
